EXPERIENCES WITH GENERAL CELLULAR AND NEURAL CELLULAR PATHOLOGY IN A CASE BASED BLENDED LEARNING ECOSYSTEM’S CBBLE”"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEhYaBNmzXJnYsni4LI14NNAoE20AnbaIPy-Fk0ktgvj3EruluKFzCgAyYJETnjovE4OqTDdNu5lotn2dxI9J_zlbrgyWzPby7Vd6ECsWDRkwWHQWPsYyj6jm1s-_m09gGyDAF8ZKSps1rdrZuNNyJVcOCDBTasMBwPr13PPF6XPgHnhyq8M10HfmePqzQ\/s320\/IMG_1205.webp\" width=\"320\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHello everyone,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI am Saptarshi Saha, a 4th year medical student studying MBBS Jinan University in China. As a medical student, my journey has been full of ups and downs, excitement and surprises, but one of the most impactful and thrilling experience for me has been writing, preparing and presenting medical case reports (like painting the real life portrait of an individual).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEach individual is unique and every“body” has something new to tell. Preparing case reports is what I believe to be the best way to deal with medical issues and gain deep insights into healthcare problems. So, in this blog I invite you to be my companion in this journey to explore few of the many interesting cases from my portfolio, which I got the opportunity to prepare till date under the guidance of my esteemed professor Dr. Rakesh Sir (HOD medicine KIMS) and my Seniors whose valuable inputs have made my learning experience much more impactful.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI welcome all the readers to explore these case reports with me as a method of learning and to contribute to the growing database of medical knowledge. Patients and their particular circumstances are unique, and these case reports are useful in helping healthcare providers tailor their assessment and treatment to accommodate such individual needs.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt the end I would like to say that most of the case reports were done through telephonic conversation from 2000 miles away. Still, I had tried my level best to paint these live portraits as carefully in a detailed manner as possible.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESo, without further ado let’s get started.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E——\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFeb 11 2022, no it’s not my birthday. It’s the day when this journey began. I was sitting in my room, leafing through the pages of Netter’s atlas when at around 6:45 pm my senior called me saying “Saptarshi, \u0026nbsp;can you help us prepare the case report of this man who hails from your state and speaks your mother tongue?”. Without giving it a second thought I said “yes please”. Though the case was not a very complicated one, I had an invaluable experience and learnt a lot because it was my first case report filing.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELet’s have a look…..\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe was a male patient, aged 33 years. Seeing me speak his mother tongue he was quite delighted and eagerly shared all his details which helped a novice like me file a detailed case history which was quite fundamental for arriving at a final diagnosis within a short period of time.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe first thing that caught my attention was the mild swelling of his left cheek. He complained of pus oozing out from the upper left posterior teeth region especially while sneezing or lying down for the past 1 and a half month accompanied with pain and swelling.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn examination of oral cavity pus point seen posterior to 3rd molar in the left upp. gingival area. Active pus discharge seen on pressing upper gingival sulcus, region distal to 27. On palpation, bulging and tenderness present in left gingivobuccal sulcus lateral to canine.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFurther radiological investigation suggestive of left maxillary sinusitis with osteomyelitis changes in the left floor and medial and lateral borders of the maxillary sinus. Pro antral communication distal to #28 region.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEnterococcus and fusobacterium species grown in pus culture.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;CECT neck revealed an expansive unilocular lytic lesion involving the maxillary arch on the left side building in the lumen of the left maxillary sinus. The lesion was causing significant narrowing of the maxillary sinus and reaching up to orbital floor superiorly. Significant cortical thickening was noted with multiple areas of cortical break involving the posterior and anterior superior aspect.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA provisional diagnosis of Left oroantral fistula with chronic maxillary sinusitis, left spheroid degeneration with Denovo DM type II was made.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistopathological features of the biopsy sample suggestive of inflammatory lesions.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESurgery executed: Enucleation and curettage of the cyst\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPostoperative diagnosis of odontogenic cyst was made.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe detailed case report can be found in the link given below\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/ssahamedicalcases.blogspot.com\/2022\/02\/33-yr-old-male-with-co-pus-oozing-out.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/ssahamedicalcases.blogspot.com\/2022\/02\/33-yr-old-male-with-co-pus-oozing-out.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt that time though I only had some vague idea about odontogenic cysts, I knew nothing about it’s treatment and management plan nor about the above mentioned surgical procedure. To have a first hand experience about knowing the treatment flow of a patient from the time he comes to the hospital till getting discharged and even afterwards, was a valuable learning experience for me.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis was the article that helped me at that time to learn more about odontogenic cyst.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.google.co.in\/url?sa=t\u0026amp;rct=j\u0026amp;q=\u0026amp;esrc=s\u0026amp;source=web\u0026amp;cd=\u0026amp;ved=2ahUKEwjZkbTf0JT_AhWB9rsIHUYjARAQFnoECAwQAw\u0026amp;url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Fbooks%2FNBK574529%2F%23%3A~%3Atext%3DOdontogenic%2520cysts%2520are%2520usually%2520identified%2Cthey%2520cannot%2520be%2520differentiated%2520radiographically.\u0026amp;usg=AOvVaw10agRGxlrtsF74n3HgMMi1\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.google.co.in\/url?sa=t\u0026amp;rct=j\u0026amp;q=\u0026amp;esrc=s\u0026amp;source=web\u0026amp;cd=\u0026amp;ved=2ahUKEwjZkbTf0JT_AhWB9rsIHUYjARAQFnoECAwQAw\u0026amp;url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Fbooks%2FNBK574529%2F%23%3A~%3Atext%3DOdontogenic%2520cysts%2520are%2520usually%2520identified%2Cthey%2520cannot%2520be%2520differentiated%2520radiographically.\u0026amp;usg=\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENow, moving on to case 2. This one has an interesting story.....I was walking down the corridor with my friends when I saw a group of young Doctors standing around a bed. And Sir, was explaining something to them...Seeing he Sir said, \"Saptarshi, have a look...this is one interesting case, you must try to write a report on him\"... The first thing which caught my attention was that even though he was lying down in supine position without any pillow under his head his head, his head appeared to be floating mid-air and his legs were fixed in a flexed position. Sir, explained that he can neither lower his head nor extend his legs rendering him incapable of walking. For the past 7 years he has been confined to bed or chair.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELater, a detailed history taking revealed a lot of interesting facts.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is the life story of a 65 years old man who was a toddy climber by profession until various health ailments crippled him. In the year 2002, surgery for rt. renal calculi was done. In 2007, ORIF was done for rt. femur #. In 2012, tibia # but no treatment done. In 2013, hip # no treatment sought because of poor financial conditions. Unable to walk since then. He used to do as limited movement as possible otherwise his pain would flare up. In 2015, diagnosed with fixed flexion deformity grade 3 of both knees with bilateral knee pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn 2022, he came to us with complaints of anuria, urinary urgency and incomplete voiding of urine. Also complained of SOB grade 2 and there were signs of pedal edema.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENCCT-KUB detected bilateral ureteric calculi causing moderate hydroureteronephrosis, prostatomegaly, left renal calculi 4 mm size.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EXray of the neck and knee joints revealed cervical ankylosis and fixed flexion deformity of knee joints.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfter medications and 2 sessions of hemodialysis, his urine output increased. A diagnosis of postrenal AKI secondary to B\/L ureteric calculi was made. Patient was recommended to undergo surgery but concent was not given. Hence pateint was discharged.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThough the patient left us...he left us with a lot of questions which remained unanswered.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAs we can see this patient is suffering from recurrent renal stones, multiple fractures (indicating weak and brittle bones) from time to time, so I tried to find out if there is any correlation between his ailments and whether fluorosis is the cause of all this problems.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn the below attached link I have done my level best to gather and compiled together all the available information to arrive at a final conclusion. Please have a look....\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/ssahamedicalcases.blogspot.com\/2022\/02\/fluorosis-and-renal-stones.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/ssahamedicalcases.blogspot.com\/2022\/02\/fluorosis-and-renal-stones.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMoving on to the final case…\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENOTE: this case history was taken via a telephonic conversation which denied me the opportunity to do first-hand physical examination on this patient.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis is the story of a 49 yr old man...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 2000, one day while watching TV in the club room, he felt the back of his neck and head getting stiff along with the involuntary movement of his head in a \"no-no\" fashion (at first only visible on careful observation). It lasted for 5-10 secs and happened 1-2 times in a day, a few times a wk, accompanied by a prickling pin and needle sensation along his spine sometimes.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWithin few years (2005) the frequency, duration (10-15 mins), and severity increased progressively. A local physician prescribed medication but no relief.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOnce while in a market with his employee, he c\/o these same symptoms, unable to carry on with the intended work, he sat down. Since that incident, he unwillingly had to pass on more responsibilities to the employees.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWent to Bangalore in 2006, Dr. prescribed Tryptomer 0.25 mg and Lonazep 0.5 mg o.d, taking those provided complete relief for 3 months. Then again it started increasing.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe tried homeopathic treatment, which provided no relief.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWent to Bangalore again in 2008, Dr told him to increase the dosage if req. Doing so provided some relief.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThen he lost contact with his treating Dr and since medicines were becoming less and less effective day by day, he stopped taking those. In the meantime, his symptoms kept on becoming more severe.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe c\/o not being able to have proper sleep because whenever, he would lie down in a supine position his involuntary head movement would reappear, so much so that he had to lie down on his sides with a pillow below his head and they went to sleep. In most cases, he failed to get any sleep. Medications by Drs for not being able to sleep did little help.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBy 2012, he was not able to maintain balance and was past pointing test +ve (if asked to touch his nose he will touch his eyes instead). He went to Bhopal, Dr did MRI, and diagnosed it to be Spino cerebellar degeneration. Dr. prescribed Liofen 5mg and Clonafit 0.5 MD. But, for a few months, his symptoms reduced a bit, then again like before.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 2012, he did Ayurveda treatment as his speech was getting slurry. He chewed the roots of the plant \"long pepper\" till 2016, which he claims to have improved his speech. Before which it was incomprehensible.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBy 2013, he was unable to walk without someone's help or support.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBy 2015-16, he can't even go downstairs to sit in his shop below his house. In the meantime, he was recurring huge losses in his business, since he had handed the responsibility to the employees.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETill July 2016, he took medications, then gave up since taking those made no difference.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe became confined to his room mostly, sometimes would rarely visit his friend's home nearby (booking an auto from the front gate to reach his friend's house).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 2018, when his family separated, his BP became very high. Dr diagnosed HTN and since then taking Telvas AM o.d.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFor the past 3 yrs, c\/o constipation (no defecation for a day or so, hence uses laxatives sometimes ). No digestive issues.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt present, pt is not able to write properly, head movement would happen more when he is doing puja (meditation), watching phone, urinating or defecating, or if stressed out or thinking deeply. But, if he tries to sleep, his head movement stops.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPt had now attached metal rods all around and inside his house, which he uses to walk around. He reported doing exercise does provide some relief.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAlso there is an interesting psychosocial component to it, which can be found in the link given below.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/ssahamedicalcases.blogspot.com\/2023\/02\/patient-history-pt-is-49-yrs-old-male.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/ssahamedicalcases.blogspot.com\/2023\/02\/patient-history-pt-is-49-yrs-old-male.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESince the time he was diagnosed with autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia, his last and only wish is the discovery of a magic pill that can treat his condition and make him return to normal life.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESo, the question which pegged me is how do we manage this kind of patients?\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMy search for an answer lead me to this article.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.google.co.in\/url?sa=t\u0026amp;rct=j\u0026amp;q=\u0026amp;esrc=s\u0026amp;source=web\u0026amp;cd=\u0026amp;ved=2ahUKEwjbhJLC6pb_AhUNmIsKHRAIDWYQFnoECBYQAQ\u0026amp;url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Fpmc%2Farticles%2FPMC6089349%2F\u0026amp;usg=AOvVaw2wDvB5yI4t8tJjr8qcuPbF\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.google.co.in\/url?sa=t\u0026amp;rct=j\u0026amp;q=\u0026amp;esrc=s\u0026amp;source=web\u0026amp;cd=\u0026amp;ved=2ahUKEwjbhJLC6pb_AhUNmIsKHRAIDWYQFnoECBYQAQ\u0026amp;url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Fpmc%2Farticles%2FPMC6089349%2F\u0026amp;usg=AOvVaw2wDvB5yI4t8tJjr8qcuPbF\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;As we all know till date hereditary ataxia has no effective treatment and management remains supportive and symptomatic.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn our case how did we manage the patient....well, to support our patient though he is far away from us we created an individualized PaJR group (like we had done for many of our patients)...it helps us keep a track of our patients who need a long term health support.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EEveryday this man describes his day's events helping us gauze his condition. He does household chores and physical exercise which even though is not going to cure him....is slowing down his disease progression which is evident from his daily life activities.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENow, it is our responsibility as medical students and researchers to find out that magic pill this patient and many others like him are eagerly waiting for to help them return back to the normal life they want.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E______\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELast few words.....before I end.\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFrom my experience I can say medical case reports provide an opportunity to learn from real-life situations and can increase awareness among healthcare providers concerning particular conditions. It also supplements the associate with scientific advancements by analyzing the results of treatments and the effects of drugs on clinical cases.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETo see a patient come to us suffering and leave with a smile on their face is an indescribable feeling. Knowing that I have had even a small part to play in relieving their pain and discomfort brings me so much joy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBeing able to help people and make a difference in their lives is what makes this profession so special. Nothing can bring more happiness than the knowledge that you have helped someone end their suffering........\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWith this I end here for now....Thank you if you had stayed with me until the end.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr yrs old female w\/c\/o recurrent ulcers, pain on rt knee and hip"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPATIENT HISTORY:\u003C\/b\u003E Pt is a 52 yrs old female, working as a school teacher.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EBIOLOGICAL COMPONENT:\u003C\/u\u003E Since childhood, the patient suffers from constipation (2-3days later incomplete defecation, hard stool)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt the age of 19, she c\/o heavy bleeding while passing stool followed by splinter hemorrhagic pain 1-2 hrs after defecation of hard stool which made it impossible to sit also. The doctor prescribed medications that stopped the bleeding. Now, no more bleeding, only when suffering from constipation c\/o pain while defecating.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 1999, she started c\/o a continuous whole right side pain (from head to toe) which would intensify on working and at night while going to sleep(the pain would be so severe that she could not fall asleep also sometimes). After suffering for a few months and taking medicines from a local Doctor slight relief. She went to Vellore to seek further advice where Doctor said the pain was due to some minor neuropathic problem. Medications were prescribed taking which would provide temporary relief. Sought no further treatment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHypothyroidism was detected while she was in Vellore. Since then taking Thyronorm tab. (first few years 50 mcg then 100 mcg).\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn the year 2014, after reading an article about breasts ca. she did a self-examination. She thought she could feel a lump in the lat. quadrant of rt breast. But Doctor said there is nothing. After 1 year she started c\/o pain. Dr. diagnosed it to be a fibroadenoma of the breast. In 2016 Jan, a lumpectomy was done for rt breast. Dr. said there was also a small lump in the left breast which needs no operation.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 2014-15, she started c\/o gastric problems (nausea, headache, burps, abd bloating) frequently. Endoscopy detected gastritis. Medications were prescribed taking which will cause some relief.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA few months later, she started vomiting (whatever she ate or drank, 15-16 times sometimes in a day) and sudden diffused abd pain (lasting for a few mins to hrs, frequently after fatty meal), mostly in the upper rt quadrant and center of abd spreading to the back and center of her chest. She frequently would be hospitalized. Had to keep Aciloc and Ondem inj. in the home. After staying like this for a year or two, she visited a gastroenterologist. USG revealed gallstone.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn July 2019, a cholecystectomy was done. For a few months, she was feeling alright (no more vomiting, abd pain, or gastric issues). Then again she started complaining of localized pain in the upper abd. The pain would mostly start at midnight\/dawn which would disturb her sleep. So much so that she needed painkillers. Dr. did a colonoscopy and endoscopy which revealed a colon ulcer (2020) and her Hb level was also low (Previously she had mentioned since childhood her Hb lvl always used to remain on the lower side, she claims she had no access to good quality nutritious food during childhood). The biopsy report was normal. Medication and strict control of diet were recommended (avoidance of oily spicy fried foods, avoidance of citrus foods, etc.). Following which gave her some relief for a few months.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6 months later she went for a check up and Dr said no more ulcer. Still, she went to Hyderabad for reconfirmation. They also reported no ulcers and gave Iron dextran inj. For 1 year she had no complaints.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 2020, c\/o rt shoulder pain on movement. Dr. diagnosed it as tendonitis. On doing physiotherapy the pain subsided. Earlier, she also had pain in lt shoulder which reduced on doing physiotherapy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThen in 2021, she again started c\/o localized pain in upp abd(starting at midnight, but this time less severe). Her Hb lvl again reduced a bit. Dr. performed a spiral enteroscopy. A duodenal ulcer and a colon ulcer were detected. Dr. prescribed Pentasa enema, Cremaffin syrup (since then she continues it, whenever stops again the problem of constipation) and Wysolone tab (40mg then 20 mg 10 mg 5mg finally stopped). Her biopsy report was normal.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe c\/o pain (claims it does not feel like muscle pain) in her rt hip joint since 1999, which would reduce on resting or on compression or oil massage. Doing physiotherapy for a few wks and exercising she felt no pain from Sep 2022 to Mar 2023. Now again c\/o pain which starts from her rt hip jt and travels down towards her knee. She mentioned 1-2 yrs ago Doctor diagnosed disc herniation in the lumbar spine.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFor the past 2-3 months c\/o epigastric burning sensation (can't specify any fixed pattern, lasts for only 2-3 secs, 2-3 times a wk).\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe was told to stop taking Wysolone by Physician. After she stopped Wysolone, she c\/o extreme localized stabbing epigastric pain lasting for 10 mins max. Her Hb came down to 13.2 from 14.6 gm\/dl. No further treatment was done. At present, the pain occurs 1-2 times\/wk and lasts for 2-3 secs or 1-2 mins. She also started c\/o severe pain in the rt knee (more severe after walking, climbing stairs or trying to fold her legs) and rt hip joint after stopping Wysolone. Decreases a bit at night while resting or doing a hot oil massage. She also noticed some popular rashes emerging on her face and left hand.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDenied h\/o HTN or DM. No addiction history.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMenstrual history: Menarche at age of 13-14. Menopause at 8-9 months ago. Normal regular cycle. No menorrhagia or dysmenorrhea was reported.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPSYCHOSOCIAL COMPONENT\u003C\/u\u003E: Pt belongs to a very humble family. During her childhood had no access to enough food. Her dad being lazy and not willing to work would sit idly at home. Seeing this her mother sold all her jewelry and used to do a job of sewing to make ends meet.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWhenever her mom would get a job for her father after going to work for a few days he would leave it and stayat home. These often lead to quarrels.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 1990, when she turned 18 yrs, her family decided to marry her off. At the final stage of getting married, she told her mom that she loves her Economics teacher and wants to marry him. Her mom denied giving permission. Still, she chose to marry her boyfriend (teacher) instead of the groom. Since her mom had gone through so much trouble for her and her siblings she was very upset about marrying against her will and permission.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn the day of her marriage, her to-be husband's ex came to the marriage hall to stop the marriage. Her husband and his ex both insulted her which lead to a quarrel.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1 month later, one night while going to sleep, a neighbor (female) called her husband to stay with her tonight because she was feeling lonely and scared to sleep alone in the house. This upset pt a lot. She realized this is not something new.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer husband's relationship with his father was not good hence he kicked them out of the house one day. They started living in the husband's friend's house. One night she caught her husband kissing one of their relatives. She decided to leave her husband. The husband begged for forgiveness. So, she continued staying with him.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESince at that time her husband had no fixed job, they had to depend on whatever tuition he could get. He would be busy with work and had no time for her.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA few months later she became pregnant. She went to stay in her father's room. Her husband stopped coming to visit her or keeping in touch with her. He wrote a letter saying he wants to end the marriage. She fell very ill hearing this. Then his friends talked with him and convinced him otherwise. Soon after he got a job. She gave birth to their son. He became so busy with work that he had no time to talk with her also apart from what groceries he should buy from the market. He started writing stories. On reading those he realized it is about his ex and him. She felt left out and unworthy.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIn 2011, she tried committing suicide by hanging herself. Her husband saved her at the nick of time. A family meeting was arranged to resolve everything. She requested him to spend some time with her and give up writing about his ex, which again lead to many quarrels and fights. Her husband started spending some time with her.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2 yrs later she gave birth to their daughter. She realized that she needs to do a job to support her family and gain importance in her family. She soon got a job.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2-3 yrs ago, once she got to know from a relative that he had posted a writeup in social media about him and his ex. She felt very upset and tried ending her life by taking an overdose of sleeping pills. Luckily, her attempt failed.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1 yr ago, she got to know from an acquaintance that her husband has been stopped with his ex. In the meantime, by his way of speaking and through his poems she realized he had fallen in deeper love with his ex. He started ignoring her completely.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPt confronted him and explained everything from the beginning. Her husband finally understood her situation and since last one year is looking after her, and sending time with her.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe claimed to be under severe stress and mental pressure for the past 1 year, Now she is happy.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer relationship with her daughter is very good. They want to get her married first before their son but are not able to.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer relationship with her son is not that good. They wanted him to marry later but his girlfriend is putting pressure on him to get married. Also, both of their children do private jobs. This is also causing a lot of stress and tension for her.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINT ANF PT REQ\u003C\/b\u003E: 1) c\/o recurrent ulcers (?stress ulcers)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2) Pain in rt knee joint for the past 1 yr aggravated for the past few days, restricting her movements\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3) recurrent pain in rt hip jt since 1999, aggravated since past few days, restricting her movements\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4) c\/o painful inflammation of glands in the neck (?tonsils) accompanied by papular rashes on the face and hand\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4)She is fed up with following such a strict diet. Wants to lift most diet restrictions\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFAMILY HISTORY: \u003C\/b\u003EFather - HTN\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMom - shoulder pain, died at age 48 (suicide)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMom's dad - DM, died due to kidney failure\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EYounger sister - shoulder pain\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDIET: সকাল সাড়ে সাতটা ও সন্ধ্যা ৬টায় লাল চায়ের সঙ্গে মুড়ি-খই মিশিয়ে।\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eসকাল ১০টা, দুপুর ২ টা, রাত ১০টায় তাজা মাছের পাতলা (তেল, মশলা কম দিয়ে) ঝোল বা পাতলা মুশুরি ডাল আর কোয়াস,আলু, গাঁজর দিয়ে সবজি।\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eএছাড়া কলা-মুড়ি বা ইদানিং তরমুজ কিংবা সকাল সাতটার আশেপাশে দুটো মেরী বিস্কুট।\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Eএই diet দুই মাস থেকে চলছে।\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBefore that, as instructed by Doctor didn't drink milk for the past 1.5 yrs. But later started consuming milk too. Her diet included everything ranging from healthy to oily spicy fried food till 2 months ago.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca yrs old female w\/c\/o stuffy nose"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;NOTE: THIS IS AN ONLINE E LOGBOOK TO DISCUSS OUR PATIENT'S DE-IDENTIFIED HEALTH DATA SHARED AFTER TAKING HIS \/ HER \/GUARDIAN'S SIGNED INFORMED CONSENT. HERE WE DISCUSS OUR INDIVIDUAL PATIENT'S PROBLEMS THROUGH A SERIES OF INPUTS FROM THE AVAILABLE GLOBAL ONLINE COMMUNITY OF EXPERTS INTENDING TO SOLVE THOSE CLINICAL PROBLEMS WITH COLLECTIVE CURRENT BEST EVIDENCE-BASED INPUT.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPATIENT HISTORY: Pt is a 9 yrs old female\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETill the age of 6-7 yrs, she c\/o constipation (2 days no defecation), passing very hard stool. Dr prescribed high fibre diet taking which normalised her bowel movement.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt that time only, she also used to c\/o digestive issues (acid reflux, sour burps, sour aftertaste, foul smell from mouth) on eating something fried, oily and spicy. Now the frequency has decreased a lot after starting high fibre diet and taking lot of water.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESince childhood, she used to suffer often from cough and cold (nasal congestion and dry cough), would last for 8-10 days, happening 2-3 times\/yr, mostly during winter months or while in AC during summer.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAt the age of 5-6 yrs, she c\/o swallowing difficulty and throat pain, stuffy nose. Dr told that her tonsils are inflamed and she should avoid catching cold at any cost. To relief nasal blockage nasal drops were prescribed which caused some relief.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFor the past one year, she c\/o severe nasal stuffiness on catching cold. She would wake up at night because of not being able to breath and using nasal drop provides no relief. Have to breathe via mouth. This worsens at night while sleeping. Even when her cough and cold is gone her stuffy mose would stay as it is. While trying to exhale air forcefully she would c\/o tearing sensation in nosal mucosa. Also, her mom noticed a very foul smell from her mouth.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis continued till Oct. She visited a Dr who said her tonsils are infected and prescribed antibiotics with nasal drop. After taking antibiotics for 20 days, the bad smell from her mouth went away and no relief from nasal blockage.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn Feb 15th she was taken to another Dr who did an Xray and diagnosed it as enlarged adenoids. Prescribed antibiotics and recommended Sx if medicines fail to cure it.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDr recommended her to keep something in mouth and try breathing via nose. But, she is not able to do it.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThis has affected her normal life also. Like she finds it hard to do dancing and exercises because of this stuffy nose.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHas a good appetite.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINT AND PT REQ.: c\/o severe stuffy nose for the past 1 yr.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPt only able to breathe via mouth\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFAMILY HISTORY:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMom - hypothyroidism detected 5 months after first delivery, took antidepressants for 2 months 1 yr after first delivery, migraine, GB Sx (5-6 yrs ago), tenosynovitis rt hand and wrist(6 months). Both babies via Cesarian delivery.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFather - reported no health issues\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EYounger Brother - reported no health issues\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDAILY ROUTINE - wake up at 7 am gets ready for school, have half glass milk with horlicks after half n hr 1 roti with any sabji.. Go school at 8.15.. Have some tiffin at 10.30,comes back home at 1.30.. Have her lunch at 2 pm l rice dal and sabji like papaya and aloo.. Goes for tution and comes back at 5pm. Again milk with biscuit or chocos.. Have her dinner around 8.30 with sometimes oats with veg soups or sometimes roti sabji.. Sometimes eats eggs in the evening or any outside snacks.. Including chips and choclates in the evening time.. Goes to bed at 9.30 or 10 pm..\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESaturday Sunday she goes for dance class in the evening for 2 hours..\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
